summary: Private SSH-tunnel proxying strips tenant header, causing 403 on scheduled jobs and admin API
description:
Issue summary:
Finovia reports intermittent 403s from the admin API and scheduled worker jobs when requests are routed through their SSH bastion using SOCKS5 dynamic forwarding. Direct requests (not going through the SSH tunnel) succeed.

Impact:
- Immediate: Several scheduled consumer jobs fail with 403 for ~12 hours during business hours, causing backlog in payment reconciliation.
- Scope: All API calls that traverse the customer's SSH bastion (SOCKS5/SSH -D) path to the private deployment. Web console sessions from corporate network appear unaffected.

Environment:
- Private deployment in us-east-1, customer-managed bastion host, NLB -> edge-proxy (customer VPC) -> Redwood private control plane.
- Edge Proxy version: v1.14.3 (customer fork).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) ssh -D 1080 bastion@bastion.finovia.internal -i ~/.ssh/bastion_key
2) export ALL_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080
3) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant-Id: finovia-prod" https://private-api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/roles
4) Observe: 403 returned. Repeat same curl without ALL_PROXY set -> 200 OK.

Relevant logs (edge-proxy access log snippet):
- Incoming request from 10.0.34.12 via TCP proxied by bastion (X-Forwarded-For present). Access log shows downstream headers: "X-Tenant-Id" missing and "Authorization" present.
- Gateway auth check: "missing tenant header -> authz denied"

Notes:
- Customer asserts this started after a bastion container upgrade to alpine:3.18 two weeks ago, though timing is approximate.
- All failing requests share path/transport characteristic: proxied via SOCKS5 dynamic forwarding.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:04 - Laura Chen (Support): Customer first reported failure; provided curl reproducer and access logs. Marked P1 due to payment reconciliation impact.
2026-03-10 12:10 - Miguel Rivera (SRE): Ack. Reproduced locally by spinning up an SSH dynamic forward. Observed header drop when using socks5 proxy from OpenSSH client -> likely not a token issue.
2026-03-11 09:22 - Finovia (Customer): Provided tcpdump from bastion showing HTTP/1.1 request intact before local proxy, header appears removed once forwarded to NLB.

2026-03-12 15:48 - Miguel Rivera (SRE): Performed controlled test: using HTTP CONNECT proxy (squid) preserved X-Tenant-Id; using ssh -D (socks5) dropped the header along the path. Hypothesis: local bastion process is re-originating requests and not forwarding custom headers for proxied TCP streams.
2026-03-13 08:37 - Support (Laura Chen): Customer applied temporary workaround (use corporate HTTP proxy or explicit port-forwarding with ssh -L) and confirmed scheduled jobs resumed.

2026-03-13 14:02 - Engineering (Rohit Patil): Agreed to patch edge-proxy to detect missing tenant header and consult fallback tenant mapping based on source IP and configured tenant CIDR maps. Filed INT follow-up for implementation and docs update.
investigation_notes: 10-Mar: Reproduced using local ssh -D to a publicly accessible test endpoint. Observed that a socks5 stream ends up being re-originated by the bastion's user-space agent, which strips non-standard headers when building the upstream HTTP request.
11-Mar: Bastion tcpdump shows the original client sends X-Tenant-Id to local SOCKS proxy; the proxy then issues a new HTTP request without X-Tenant-Id when performing the outbound connection.
11-Mar: Differences between HTTP CONNECT (preserves raw TCP) and SOCKS5 dynamic forwarding (application-level proxy) explain why header is lost only for ssh -D flows.

12-Mar: Confirmed edge-proxy correctly rejects requests with missing tenant header per RBAC rules. No misconfiguration found in RBAC policy. The root cause is header omission upstream by the customer's bastion/proxying layer.

12-Mar: Customer identifies upgrade on bastion which replaced a small helper (sproxy) with a newer default that rebuilds requests. We saw consistent reproduction with the customer's helper binary in a containerized environment.

13-Mar: Risk assessment: Long-term, many customers use SSH bastions; difference between HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5 needs clearer documentation. Edge-proxy fallback (based on source IP mapping) can mitigate but has security implications; will implement as opt-in and logged heavily.
resolution:
Workaround provided: customer switched scheduled jobs to use port-forwarding (ssh -L) or corporate HTTP proxy (CONNECT) which preserved X-Tenant-Id; scheduled jobs resumed.

Short-term mitigation: Support updated customer runbook to prefer HTTP CONNECT proxies or explicit L7 proxies that preserve headers for service-to-service calls.

Long-term fix: Engineering to implement optional "tenant-source-ip-mapping" fallback in edge-proxy to allow mapping a source IP/CIDR to a tenant when a tenant header is absent (opt-in per-customer config). INT ticket created to track the implementation and security review (INT-2201).

Follow-ups:
- INT-2201: Design + implementation of tenant-source-ip-mapping (security review required).
- Docs update: add guidance to Private Deployment onboarding about SSH bastion behaviors and recommended proxying modes (Confluence page linked).
- Post-incident: check other private customers for similar SSH-bastion upgrades and proactively notify.

Status: In Progress - short-term workaround validated by customer; engineering design in progress.
